answer: Each agent earns access to valuable tasks only after posting a bond that is slashed if its work fails independent checks; rewards accrue gradually with a track record, not at account creation. This makes a swarm of fresh identities costly: the attacker must lock up capital for every agent and risks losing it when claims are challenged. A whisper network can flag suspicious clusters, but it cannot replace verification; nectar and jade are merely labels, not proof of personhood.
